## Agent Runtime

| Tool | Description | Permission |
|------|-------------|--------------------------|
| [`delete_workspace`](#delete_workspace) | Permanently delete a retained runtime workspace and all of its files. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`read_workspace_file`](#read_workspace_file) | Read a file from your Agent Runtime's retained workspace using its run_id. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`transfer_workspace_file`](#transfer_workspace_file) | Copy a file between this machine and a Remote Agent's workspace without reading it. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`write_workspace_file`](#write_workspace_file) | Create a file in your Agent Runtime's retained workspace using its run_id. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`start_agent_run`](#start_agent_run) | Start a background run on an Agent that has Agent Runtime. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`get_agent_run`](#get_agent_run) | Read a run's state, the result it has handed back so far, and whether it accepts a follow-up. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`list_agent_runs`](#list_agent_runs) | List recent runs on one or more accessible Agents, newest first. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`steer_agent_run`](#steer_agent_run) | Send one message to a run: a course correction to a live run without stopping the work, or, when the run has finished and its workspace is retained, a follow-up that continues the SAME run and save... | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`cancel_agent_run`](#cancel_agent_run) | Stop an active run. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`post_agent_run_message`](#post_agent_run_message) | Post a brief update to the Slack thread an active Agent Runtime run reports to. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`post_agent_run_file`](#post_agent_run_file) | Upload a file into the messaging-channel thread a run reports to — a demo recording, for example — so it renders natively there (Slack plays video uploads inline). | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`transfer_credential`](#transfer_credential) | Give a Remote Agent a credential, so a handed-over task can use the CLI authentication the local session was using. | [`credential:create`](/docs/reference/permissions#credential:create) |

### start_agent_run

Required RBAC permission: [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read)

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `agent_id` | `string` | No | The agent to do the work (UUID or agent__<slug> tool name). Omit when calling through an MCP gateway to select an assigned runtime subagent using the gateway's load-balancing policy, or pass a load-balanced router agent to select from its assigned runtime subagents. |
| `exclude_agent_ids` | `string[]` | No | Runtime subagents that already failed on a previous attempt for this request, to skip when selecting a fallback on an MCP gateway. |
| `credential_grant_ids` | `string[]` | No | One-time credential_grant_id handles minted by transfer_credential({ ephemeral: true }). Consumed at launch and bound only to the winning runtime pod. |
| `message` | `string` | Yes | What the agent should do, including handoff context and acceptance criteria. |
| `attachments` | `object[]` | No | Input files staged before the first turn. For repository work, include a patch for uncommitted changes and identify the base commit in message. Never include credentials. |
| `attachments[].name` | `string` | Yes |  |
| `attachments[].contentType` | `string` | Yes |  |
| `attachments[].contentBase64` | `string` | Yes |  |
| `limits` | `object` | No | Limits for this run, each at or below the Agent's own (for the tier, its largest tier); a larger value is refused with the maximum named. Omit to take the Agent's defaults. |
| `limits.tier` | `string` | No | The name of one of the organization's runtime tiers, at or below this Agent's scaleup tier. Choose by size, not by name: inside a run, $ARCHESTRA_AGENT_RUNTIME_TIERS lists the tiers the run may move to with their CPU, memory and workspace size; pick the smallest that covers the work. To move work to another tier, start a run of the same Agent at that tier and hand over the branch. A tier above the scaleup tier is refused with the allowed tiers and their sizes named. |
| `limits.min_cpu` | `number` | No | CPUs the work needs. The run gets the smallest tier this Agent may use with at least this many and no smaller workspace than the Agent's default tier; refused with the allowed tiers named when none has. Use this when the tier names are unknown. |
| `limits.min_memory_gib` | `number` | No | GiB of memory the work needs, with the same effect as min_cpu. |
| `limits.idle_timeout_minutes` | `integer` | No |  |
| `limits.max_duration_hours` | `integer` | No | Hours until the run and its saved files end. Keep it short for work that nobody continues. |
| `limits.max_cost_usd` | `integer` | No |  |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `run` | `object` | Yes |  |
| `run.run_id` | `string` | Yes | Stable handle for every follow-up: get_agent_run, steer_agent_run, cancel_agent_run and the workspace file tools. |
| `run.state` | `string` | Yes | submitted \| working \| input-required \| completed \| canceled \| failed |
| `run.agent_id` | `string \| null` | Yes | The agent doing the work. |
| `run.agent_name` | `string \| null` | No | Display name of the agent doing the work, when known. |
| `run.status_reason` | `string \| null` | Yes | Why the run is in its state, when there is something to say. |
| `run.failure` | `object \| null` | Yes | Machine-readable failure of a failed run: a stable code and whether a new run of the same Agent is likely to succeed unchanged. Null otherwise. |
| `run.failure.code` | `string` | Yes |  |
| `run.failure.retriable` | `boolean` | Yes |  |
| `run.created_at` | `string` | Yes | ISO 8601. |
| `run.state_changed_at` | `string` | Yes | ISO 8601 of the last transition. |
| `run_url` | `string` | Yes | Open the run and its workspace in the browser. |
| `limits` | `object \| null` | Yes |  |
| `limits.tier` | `string \| null` | Yes | The name of the runtime tier the run has, as the organization sizes it. |
| `limits.idle_timeout_minutes` | `number` | Yes |  |
| `limits.max_duration_hours` | `number` | Yes | The run and its saved files end this many hours after the start. |
| `limits.max_cost_usd` | `number \| null` | Yes |  |
| `limits.workspace_gib` | `number` | No | The size of the run's workspace volume in GiB. Absent for a workspace from before sizes were recorded. |
| `next_step` | `string` | Yes | What to do now. |

### transfer_credential

Required RBAC permission: [`credential:create`](/docs/reference/permissions#credential:create)

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `agent_id` | `string` | No | The Agent to give the credential to (UUID or agent__<slug> tool name). Omit when calling through an MCP gateway to transfer the credential to all runtime subagents assigned to the gateway, or pass a load-balanced router agent to target its assigned runtime subagents. |
| `environment` | `object[]` | Yes | Exactly one credential to transfer. Never include more than the task needs. |
| `environment[].key` | `string` | Yes | Environment variable name, e.g. AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. |
| `environment[].type` | `"secret"` | Yes | Always 'secret'. Marks the value for redaction in logs. |
| `environment[].value` | `string` | No | The credential value to transfer. OMIT IT to declare the credential without a value and get back a link the person opens to paste it themselves — the value then never enters your context. Send a value only when the person asked you to move one you already hold. |
| `label` | `string` | No | Human-readable name shown in the Agent's credential list. Defaults to the key. |
| `ephemeral` | `boolean` | No | When true, mints a short-lived one-time credential_grant_id handle instead of persisting the secret in the database or mutating subagent declarations. Pass the returned credential_grant_id to start_agent_run so the secret is bound only to the single winning subagent pod. |
| `ttl_seconds` | `integer` | No | Optional TTL in seconds (30–3600, default 300) for an ephemeral credential grant. Implies ephemeral: true. |

#### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `key` | `string` | Yes | The environment variable the value is stored under. |
| `scope` | `"personal"` | Yes | Who the value applies to. Always personal to the calling user. |
| `declarationCreated` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether this call declared the credential on the Agent. |
| `valueStored` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether a value is now stored. False means the credential is declared and still empty. |
| `url` | `string \| null` | Yes | Where the person pastes the value. Null when this call already stored one. |
| `urls` | `string[]` | No | All per-subagent setup links when declaring a credential across multiple subagents. |
| `ephemeral` | `boolean` | No | True when the credential was minted as a short-lived one-time grant instead of stored in the database. |
| `credential_grant_id` | `string \| null` | No | One-time credential grant handle to pass to start_agent_run when ephemeral is true. |
| `expires_in_seconds` | `integer` | No | Seconds until the ephemeral credential grant expires. |
| `availability` | `string` | Yes | When a run can read the value, in plain words. |
| `next_step` | `string` | No | What to do with `url`: hand it over in the reply text, never inside a question form. Only set while a value is still missing. |

## Agents

| Tool | Description | Permission |
|------|-------------|--------------------------|
| [`create_agent`](#create_agent) | Create a new agent with the specified name, optional description, labels, prompts, icon emoji, model, explicit tool assignments, and sub-agent delegations. | [`agent:create`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:create) |
| [`get_agent`](#get_agent) | Get a specific agent by ID or name. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`list_agents`](#list_agents) | List agents with optional filtering by name, provider key, or how the caller reaches them (access). | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`edit_agent`](#edit_agent) | Edit an existing agent. | `update` on the agent (granted per item) |
| [`get_agent_skill_policy`](#get_agent_skill_policy) | Read an internal agent's skill allowlist, exclusions and current revision. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) † |
| [`patch_agent_skill_policy`](#patch_agent_skill_policy) | Change an internal agent's skill activation mode, allowlist or exclusions using its current expectedRevision from get_agent_skill_policy. | `update` on the agent (granted per item) † |
| [`list_llm_models`](#list_llm_models) | List the provider API keys the caller can use and the models linked to each. | [`llmModel:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#llmModel:read) |
| [`list_hooks`](#list_hooks) | List an agent's lifecycle hooks. | [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read) |
| [`create_hook`](#create_hook) | Create a lifecycle hook on an agent. | `update` on the agent (granted per item) |
| [`update_hook`](#update_hook) | Update an existing lifecycle hook: its event, file name, script content, Python requirements, or enabled state. | `update` on the agent (granted per item) |
| [`delete_hook`](#delete_hook) | Delete a lifecycle hook by ID. | `update` on the agent (granted per item) |

† This tool enforces an additional access requirement beyond its RBAC permission — see its details below.

### create_agent

Required RBAC permission: [`agent:create`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:create)

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `initialGrants` | `object[]` | No |  |
| `initialGrants[].subject` | `object` | Yes |  |
| `initialGrants[].subject.type` | `"user" \| "team" \| "serviceAccount" \| "oauthClient" \| "role" \| "organization"` | Yes |  |
| `initialGrants[].subject.id` | `string \| "*"` | Yes |  |
| `initialGrants[].actions` | `string[]` | Yes |  |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Name for the new resource. |
| `labels` | `object[]` | No | Optional key-value labels for organization and categorization. |
| `labels[].key` | `string` | Yes |  |
| `labels[].value` | `string` | Yes |  |
| `toolExposureMode` | `"full" \| "search_and_run_only"` | No | How tools should be loaded for MCP clients and models. Use 'search_and_run_only' to keep the initial tool list small while letting search_tools find assigned tools and run_tool execute them. MCP gateways defer skill, file, sandbox, run lifecycle and policy-management capabilities in this mode; questions and guardrails session/peer-message controls remain directly available. search_tools summarizes the caller's available built-in capability groups as well as connected MCP servers. Manual gateways also keep explicitly assigned MCP App UI tools available for client rendering. Internal chat keeps assigned skill discovery/loading, file, sandbox and run lifecycle tools directly available for its skill activation and file guidance. App tools (scaffold_app, edit_app, read_app, render_app, list_apps, and the rest of the app surface) are reached through search_tools/run_tool in 'search_and_run_only' mode. |
| `accessAllTools` | `boolean` | No | Allow dynamic tool access: search_tools/run_tool may discover and run any tool the calling user can access (MCP catalog tools and knowledge sources) without assigning it to the agent. Enabling this forces toolExposureMode to 'search_and_run_only', since dynamic access only works through the search/run dispatch surface. Defaults to false. Also gated by the organization's security settings. |
| `accessAllSubagents` | `boolean` | No | Allow dynamic subagent delegation: the agent may delegate to any internal agent the calling user can access, beyond explicitly-configured delegation targets (minus subagent exclusions). Defaults to false. |
| `subagentLoadBalancing` | `object \| null` | No | Optional subagent load-balancing and automatic failover policy across assigned runtime subagents. |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.enabled` | `boolean` | No |  |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.algorithm` | `"round_robin" \| "weighted" \| "random"` | No |  |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.weights` | `object` | No |  |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.retries` | `integer` | No |  |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.fallbackEnabled` | `boolean` | No |  |
| `description` | `string \| null` | No | Optional human-readable description of the agent. |
| `icon` | `string \| null` | No | Optional emoji icon for the agent. |
| `knowledgeBaseIds` | `string[]` | No | Knowledge base IDs to assign to the agent. Use get_knowledge_bases first when you need to look up IDs by name. |
| `connectorIds` | `string[]` | No | Knowledge connector IDs to assign directly to the agent. Use get_knowledge_connectors first when you need to look up IDs by name. |
| `subAgentIds` | `string[]` | No | Agent IDs to delegate to from this newly created agent. |
| `suggestedPrompts` | `object[]` | No | Optional suggested prompts that appear in the chat UI. |
| `suggestedPrompts[].summaryTitle` | `string` | Yes | Short title shown to users for this suggested prompt. |
| `suggestedPrompts[].prompt` | `string` | Yes | Suggested prompt text users can click to start a conversation. |
| `systemPrompt` | `string \| null` | No | The system prompt that defines the agent's behavior. |
| `toolAssignments` | `object[]` | No | Explicit tool assignments to create immediately after the agent is created. |
| `toolAssignments[].toolId` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the tool to assign to the agent. |
| `toolAssignments[].resolveAtCallTime` | `boolean` | No | When true, resolve credentials and execution target at tool call time. Prefer this for builder flows. |
| `toolAssignments[].credentialResolutionMode` | `"static" \| "dynamic" \| "enterprise_managed"` | No |  |
| `toolAssignments[].mcpServerId` | `string \| null` | No | Optional MCP server installation to pin the tool to when using static credential resolution. |
| `runtime` | `object` | No | Run this agent in its own container (Agent Runtime) instead of the built-in chat harness. Pass { template } for a maintained CLI, or { image } for a custom image. Other fields override the defaults: claudeCode.authentication is 'subscription' (each user signs in with their own Claude account, the default) or 'provider' (bill through llmApiKeyId/modelId); credentials declares environment variables a run needs (users supply values later, or use transfer_credential); ttlHours, idleTimeoutMinutes, and maxCostUsd bound each run; privileged requires an agent administrator. |

| `runtime.ports` | `integer[]` | No |  |
| `runtime.environment` | `object[] \| null` | No |  |
| `runtime.credentials` | `object[] \| null` | No |  |
| `runtime.allowAgentSuppliedCredentialValues` | `boolean` | No |  |
| `runtime.claudeCode` | `object` | No |  |
| `runtime.ttlHours` | `integer \| null` | No |  |
| `runtime.maxCostUsd` | `integer \| null` | No |  |
| `runtime.idleTimeoutMinutes` | `integer \| null` | No |  |
| `runtime.template` | `"claude-code" \| "codex" \| "opencode" \| "hermes" \| "openclaw" \| "grok" \| "kimi" \| "copilot"` | No | Maintained CLI to run: 'claude-code' (Claude Code), 'codex' (Codex), 'opencode' (OpenCode), 'hermes' (Hermes), 'openclaw' (OpenClaw), 'grok' (Grok Build), 'kimi' (Kimi Code), 'copilot' (GitHub Copilot CLI). The image, launch command, and model protocol come from the template. |
| `runtime.image` | `string` | No |  |
| `runtime.command` | `string[] \| null` | No |  |
| `runtime.inferenceProtocol` | `"openai_responses" \| "openai_chat" \| "anthropic"` | No |  |
| `networkPolicy` | `object` | No | The agent's own outbound network policy for its Agent Runtime and code sandbox. It replaces the policy of the agent's environment. Requires permission to update environments. |
| `networkPolicy.egressMode` | `"off" \| "restricted" \| "unrestricted"` | Yes | unrestricted allows all outbound traffic, restricted allows only the listed destinations, off blocks all outbound traffic. |
| `networkPolicy.domainPreset` | `"none" \| "common_dependencies" \| "package_managers"` | No | Restricted mode only: a built-in domain allowlist to add (none, common_dependencies, package_managers). |
| `networkPolicy.allowedDomains` | `string[]` | No | Restricted mode only: extra allowed domains, e.g. api.github.com or *.example.com. |
| `networkPolicy.allowedCidrs` | `string[]` | No | Allowed IP ranges in CIDR notation, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8. |
| `llmApiKeyId` | `string` | No | Provider API key the agent uses. Set together with modelId. Use list_llm_models to find both. |
| `modelId` | `string` | No | Model the agent uses: the model's id from list_llm_models, not its provider name. Set together with llmApiKeyId. |

### list_agents

Required RBAC permission: [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read)

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `providerApiKeyId` | `string \| "organization-default"` | No | Filter by a configured provider key, or organization-default for agents with no pinned key or model. |
| `limit` | `integer` | No | Maximum number of agents to return. |
| `name` | `string` | No | Optional agent name filter. Use this when the user names an agent but you still need to look up the ID. |
| `access` | `string[]` | No | Only return items the caller reaches in one of these ways: mine (created by the caller), shared (shared with the caller or one of their teams), org (shared with the whole organization), others (not shared with the caller; visible only through admin access). Omit for everything the caller can read. Use ["mine"] for "my agents". |
| `shared_with` | `string[]` | No | Only return items whose own permissions grant read to one of these subjects: org (the whole organization), role:<roleId>, team:<teamId>, user:<userId>, serviceAccount:<serviceAccountId>. Omit for no filtering. |
| `owner_ids` | `string[]` | No | Only return items created by one of these user IDs. Omit for no filtering. |

#### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `total` | `number` | Yes | The total number of matching agents. |
| `hint` | `string` | Yes | Says that each agent's `tools` are that agent's own, not tools you can call. |
| `agents` | `object[]` | Yes |  |
| `agents[].id` | `string` | Yes | The agent ID. |
| `agents[].name` | `string` | Yes | The agent name. |
| `agents[].scope` | `"personal" \| "team" \| "org"` | Yes | The agent scope. |
| `agents[].executionMode` | `"runtime" \| "foreground"` | Yes | Runtime agents retain a workspace and support steering; foreground agents do not. |
| `agents[].description` | `string \| null` | Yes | The agent description, if any. |
| `agents[].resolvedLlmProviderKeyName` | `string \| null` | Yes | The configured provider-key name, or null when unconfigured. |
| `agents[].resolvedLlmModelName` | `string \| null` | Yes | The configured model name, or null when unconfigured. |
| `agents[].teams` | `object[]` | Yes | Teams attached to it. |
| `agents[].teams[].id` | `string` | Yes | The team ID. |
| `agents[].teams[].name` | `string` | Yes | The team name. |
| `agents[].labels` | `object[]` | Yes | Assigned labels. |
| `agents[].labels[].key` | `string` | Yes | The label key. |
| `agents[].labels[].value` | `string` | Yes | The label value. |
| `agents[].tools` | `object[]` | Yes |  |
| `agents[].tools[].name` | `string` | Yes | The tool name. |
| `agents[].tools[].description` | `string \| null` | Yes | The tool description, if any. |
| `agents[].knowledgeSources` | `object[]` | Yes | Assigned knowledge bases and connectors. |
| `agents[].knowledgeSources[].name` | `string` | Yes | The knowledge source name. |

| `agents[].knowledgeSources[].type` | `"knowledge_base" \| "knowledge_connector"` | Yes | Whether this source is a knowledge base or connector. |

### edit_agent

Required RBAC permission: `update` on the agent (granted per item)

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the agent to edit. Use get_agent or list_agents to look it up by name. |

| `toolAssignments[].credentialResolutionMode` | `"static" \| "dynamic" \| "enterprise_managed"` | No |  |
| `toolAssignments[].mcpServerId` | `string \| null` | No | Optional MCP server installation to pin the tool to when using static credential resolution. |
| `description` | `string \| null` | No | New description for the agent. |
| `icon` | `string \| null` | No | New emoji icon for the agent. |
| `knowledgeBaseIds` | `string[]` | No | Replace the agent's assigned knowledge bases with this set. |
| `labels` | `object[]` | No | Replace the agent's labels with this set. |
| `labels[].key` | `string` | Yes |  |
| `labels[].value` | `string` | Yes |  |
| `name` | `string` | No | New name for the agent. |
| `connectorIds` | `string[]` | No | Replace the agent's directly assigned knowledge connectors with this set. |
| `toolExposureMode` | `"full" \| "search_and_run_only"` | No | How tools should be loaded for MCP clients and models. |
| `accessAllTools` | `boolean` | No | Allow dynamic tool access: search_tools/run_tool may discover and run any tool the calling user can access without assigning it to the agent. Enabling this forces toolExposureMode to 'search_and_run_only'. |
| `accessAllSubagents` | `boolean` | No | Allow dynamic subagent delegation: the agent may delegate to any internal agent the calling user can access, beyond explicitly-configured delegation targets (minus subagent exclusions). |
| `subagentLoadBalancing` | `object \| null` | No | Optional subagent load-balancing and automatic failover policy across assigned runtime subagents. |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.enabled` | `boolean` | No |  |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.algorithm` | `"round_robin" \| "weighted" \| "random"` | No |  |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.weights` | `object` | No |  |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.retries` | `integer` | No |  |
| `subagentLoadBalancing.fallbackEnabled` | `boolean` | No |  |
| `suggestedPrompts` | `object[]` | No | Replace the agent's suggested prompts. |
| `suggestedPrompts[].summaryTitle` | `string` | Yes | Short title shown to users for this suggested prompt. |
| `suggestedPrompts[].prompt` | `string` | Yes | Suggested prompt text users can click to start a conversation. |
| `systemPrompt` | `string \| null` | No | New system prompt for the agent. |
| `runtime` | `object \| null` | No | Run this agent in its own container (Agent Runtime) instead of the built-in chat harness. Pass { template } for a maintained CLI, or { image } for a custom image. Other fields override the defaults: claudeCode.authentication is 'subscription' (each user signs in with their own Claude account, the default) or 'provider' (bill through llmApiKeyId/modelId); credentials declares environment variables a run needs (users supply values later, or use transfer_credential); ttlHours, idleTimeoutMinutes, and maxCostUsd bound each run; privileged requires an agent administrator. Replaces the whole runtime: pass every field to keep. Pass null to return the agent to the built-in chat harness. |
| `networkPolicy` | `object \| null` | No | The agent's own outbound network policy for its Agent Runtime and code sandbox. It replaces the policy of the agent's environment. Requires permission to update environments. Replaces the whole policy. Pass null to inherit the environment's policy again. |
| `networkPolicy.egressMode` | `"off" \| "restricted" \| "unrestricted"` | Yes | unrestricted allows all outbound traffic, restricted allows only the listed destinations, off blocks all outbound traffic. |
| `networkPolicy.domainPreset` | `"none" \| "common_dependencies" \| "package_managers"` | No | Restricted mode only: a built-in domain allowlist to add (none, common_dependencies, package_managers). |
| `networkPolicy.allowedDomains` | `string[]` | No | Restricted mode only: extra allowed domains, e.g. api.github.com or *.example.com. |
| `networkPolicy.allowedCidrs` | `string[]` | No | Allowed IP ranges in CIDR notation, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8. |
| `llmApiKeyId` | `string \| null` | No | Provider API key the agent uses. Set together with modelId. Use list_llm_models to find both. Pass null for both to use the default model. |
| `modelId` | `string \| null` | No | Model the agent uses: the model's id from list_llm_models, not its provider name. Set together with llmApiKeyId. Pass null for both to use the default model. |

### list_llm_models

Required RBAC permission: [`llmModel:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#llmModel:read)

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `provider` | `"openai" \| "gemini" \| "anthropic" \| "bedrock" \| "cohere" \| "cerebras" \| "mistral" \| "perplexity" \| "groq" \| "xai" \| "openrouter" \| "vllm" \| "ollama" \| "ollama-native" \| "zhipuai" \| "deepseek" \| "minimax" \| "kimi" \| "kimi-code" \| "azure" \| "github-copilot" \| "microsoft-365-copilot" \| "archestra" \| "voyage" \| "jev"` | No | Only list keys for this provider. |
| `query` | `string` | No | Only list models whose name contains this text. |

#### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `apiKeys` | `object[]` | Yes |  |
| `apiKeys[].id` | `string` | Yes | Pass as llmApiKeyId. |
| `apiKeys[].name` | `string` | Yes | The key's display name. |
| `apiKeys[].provider` | `string` | Yes | The key's LLM provider. |
| `apiKeys[].models` | `object[]` | Yes |  |
| `apiKeys[].models[].id` | `string` | Yes | Pass as modelId. |
| `apiKeys[].models[].name` | `string` | Yes | The provider's model name. |
| `apiKeys[].omittedModelCount` | `number` | Yes | Linked models left out after the first 100. Narrow with query to see them. |

### list_hooks

Required RBAC permission: [`agent:read`](/docs/reference/permissions#agent:read)

Availability: Served only when the code runtime is enabled (the same prerequisite as the [Code Sandbox](/docs/reference/archestra-mcp-server/skills-and-files#code-sandbox) tools), because a hook executes in the conversation sandbox.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `agent_id` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the agent whose hooks to list. |

#### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `hooks` | `object[]` | Yes |  |
| `hooks[].id` | `string` | Yes | The hook ID. |
| `hooks[].agentId` | `string` | Yes | The agent the hook belongs to. |
| `hooks[].event` | `"session_start" \| "pre_tool_use" \| "post_tool_use"` | Yes | The lifecycle event the hook fires on. |
| `hooks[].fileName` | `string` | Yes | The script file name (.py or .sh); also the execution-order key within an event. |
| `hooks[].content` | `string` | Yes | The script content. |
| `hooks[].requirements` | `string[]` | Yes | Python dependencies installed before a .py hook runs. |
| `hooks[].enabled` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether the hook currently fires. |
| `hooks[].createdAt` | `string` | Yes | ISO timestamp when the hook was created. |
| `hooks[].updatedAt` | `string` | Yes | ISO timestamp when the hook was last updated. |

### create_hook

Required RBAC permission: `update` on the agent (granted per item)

Availability: Served only when the code runtime is enabled (the same prerequisite as the [Code Sandbox](/docs/reference/archestra-mcp-server/skills-and-files#code-sandbox) tools), because a hook executes in the conversation sandbox.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `agent_id` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the agent to add the hook to. |
| `event` | `"session_start" \| "pre_tool_use" \| "post_tool_use"` | Yes | The lifecycle event the hook fires on: session_start, pre_tool_use, or post_tool_use. |
| `file_name` | `string` | Yes | Plain script file name ending in .py or .sh, e.g. check.py. Unique per (agent, event); hooks on the same event run in file-name order. |
| `content` | `string` | Yes | The script content. It receives the JSON payload on stdin. |
| `requirements` | `string[]` | No | Optional Python dependencies (pip requirement strings) installed before a .py hook runs. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | No | Whether the hook fires. Defaults to true. |

#### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `hook` | `object` | Yes |  |
| `hook.id` | `string` | Yes | The hook ID. |
| `hook.agentId` | `string` | Yes | The agent the hook belongs to. |
| `hook.event` | `"session_start" \| "pre_tool_use" \| "post_tool_use"` | Yes | The lifecycle event the hook fires on. |
| `hook.fileName` | `string` | Yes | The script file name (.py or .sh); also the execution-order key within an event. |
| `hook.content` | `string` | Yes | The script content. |
| `hook.requirements` | `string[]` | Yes | Python dependencies installed before a .py hook runs. |
| `hook.enabled` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether the hook currently fires. |
| `hook.createdAt` | `string` | Yes | ISO timestamp when the hook was created. |
| `hook.updatedAt` | `string` | Yes | ISO timestamp when the hook was last updated. |

### update_hook

Required RBAC permission: `update` on the agent (granted per item)

Availability: Served only when the code runtime is enabled (the same prerequisite as the [Code Sandbox](/docs/reference/archestra-mcp-server/skills-and-files#code-sandbox) tools), because a hook executes in the conversation sandbox.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the hook to update. |
| `event` | `"session_start" \| "pre_tool_use" \| "post_tool_use"` | No | Optional new lifecycle event. |
| `file_name` | `string` | No | Optional new script file name ending in .py or .sh. |
| `content` | `string` | No | Optional new script content. |
| `requirements` | `string[]` | No | Optional replacement list of Python dependencies. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | No | Optionally enable or disable the hook. |

#### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `hook` | `object` | Yes |  |
| `hook.id` | `string` | Yes | The hook ID. |
| `hook.agentId` | `string` | Yes | The agent the hook belongs to. |
| `hook.event` | `"session_start" \| "pre_tool_use" \| "post_tool_use"` | Yes | The lifecycle event the hook fires on. |
| `hook.fileName` | `string` | Yes | The script file name (.py or .sh); also the execution-order key within an event. |
| `hook.content` | `string` | Yes | The script content. |
| `hook.requirements` | `string[]` | Yes | Python dependencies installed before a .py hook runs. |
| `hook.enabled` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether the hook currently fires. |
| `hook.createdAt` | `string` | Yes | ISO timestamp when the hook was created. |
| `hook.updatedAt` | `string` | Yes | ISO timestamp when the hook was last updated. |

### delete_hook

Required RBAC permission: `update` on the agent (granted per item)

Availability: Served only when the code runtime is enabled (the same prerequisite as the [Code Sandbox](/docs/reference/archestra-mcp-server/skills-and-files#code-sandbox) tools), because a hook executes in the conversation sandbox.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | Yes | The ID of the hook to delete. |

#### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes |  |
| `id` | `string` | Yes |  |
